newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's ATX claws to new record, rally slows.
newsitem.headline: Austria's ATX claws to new record, rally slows.

text.p: Austria's ATX index nudged to a new record closing high on Friday in a session traders said was dominated by the expiry of July ATX futures.
"Today was overshadowed by the expiry. More than two thirds of orders were linked to it," said one market participant.
The 21-share blue chip ATX ended 0.94 points, or 0.07 percent, up at 1,430.23 -- the highest close since the index was recalculated in January 1991.
But the settlement was well below the intra-day high of 1,440.25 and traders said the downward correction could take prices back towards 1,410.
"I expect things to quieten down in the coming week and the ATX to settle into a 1,410 to 1,450 points range. There is room for a correction down towards 1,415 or 1,410," a trader said.
Heavily weighted utility and energy stocks appeared to have exhausted their upward potential for the time being, he added.
July ATX futures slipped 5.0 points to 1,427 on 549 contracts. August fell 12 points to 1,430 on 1,486 contracts.
Overall 12 ATX shares finished higher and nine lower.
Brewer BBAG was the biggest gainer, firming 35 schillings, or 4.41 percent, to 828.
Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien was the biggest decliner, down 11 schillings, or 2.05 percent, to 526 schillings. Traders have reported steady selling of Flughafen shares for some time.
"But I think support at 515-520 will hold and it's only a question of time before Flughafen breaks above 540 and towards 570-580," said a dealer.
The all-share Vienna bourse index ended 1.25 points, or 0.24 percent, up at 513.17.
